english.heading: Plant Selection and Guilds
body: Choose plants that work together—and change the planting as it grows.

body.text: Hlawula swimila leswi tirhaka swin'we—kutani u cinca ku byala loko swi ya swi kula.
body.backTranslation: Choose plants that work together—and then change the planting as they keep growing.

english.heading: Plant Selection and Guilds
body: A fruit tree needs light, water, soil nutrients and room. Support plants can supply food, leafy mulch, flowers and living cover.  Give each plant a useful job. Keep observing whether it helps the tree and the household. Which jobs does your planting need?

body.text: Murhi wa mihandzu wu lava ku vonakala ka dyambu, mati, nutrients ta misava ni ndhawu. Support plants swi nga nyika swakudya, mulch wa matluka, swiluva ni xifunengeto xa swimila leswi hanyaka. Nyika ximila xin'wana ni xin'wana ntirho lowu pfunaka. Tshama u langutisisa leswaku xana xi pfuna murhi ni ndyangu. Hi tihi tintirho leti ku byala ka wena ku ti lavaka?
body.backTranslation: A fruit tree needs sunlight, water, soil nutrients and space. Support plants can provide food, leaf mulch, flowers and a covering of living plants. Give each plant a helpful job. Keep watching carefully whether it helps the tree and the family. What jobs does your planting need?

english.heading: Start With the Site
body: Find out what is limiting growth before choosing a plant.

body.text: Kuma leswi hungutaka ku kula u nga si hlawula ximila.
body.backTranslation: Find what reduces growth before you choose a plant.

english.heading: Start With the Site
body: Check sunlight, drainage, soil condition and water availability. Nitrogen is only one possible limitation.  Compare the soil beneath mulch with exposed soil. Choose support plants that fit the actual conditions. What does this site need first?

body.text: Languta ku vonakala ka dyambu, ndlela leyi mati ma hundzaka ha yona ekhatsi ka misava, xiyimo xa misava ni leswaku mati ma kona. Nitrogen i xin'wana ntsena xa swilo leswi nga ha hungutaka ku kula. Fananisa misava leyi nga ehansi ka mulch ni misava leyi nga funeriwangiki. Hlawula support plants leswi fambisanaka ni swiyimo leswi nga kona hakunene. Xana ndhawu leyi yi sungula yi lava yini?
body.backTranslation: Look at how the sun shows/appears [?], the way water passes through inside the soil, the condition of the soil, and whether water is present. Nitrogen is only one of the things that can decrease growth [?: 'ku hungutaka ku kula' = decrease growing]. Compare the soil that is under mulch and soil that is not covered. Choose support plants that fit together with the conditions that are really there. What does this place begin by needing?

english.heading: Give Every Plant a Job
body: A useful guild produces benefits you can observe.

heading.text: Nyika Ximila Xin'wana Ni Xin'wana Ntirho

body.text: Guild leyi pfunaka yi humesa mimpfuno leyi u nga yi vonaka.
body.backTranslation: A guild that helps produces benefits that you can see.

english.heading: Give Every Plant a Job
body: Choose members for food, nitrogen fixation, mulch, flowers or ground cover. One plant may do several jobs.  By the end, plan a guild, explain how residues feed soil, and decide which support plants to keep, cut or remove. Which job is still missing?

heading.text: Nyika Ximila Xin'wana Ni Xin'wana Ntirho

body.text: Hlawula swirho swa guild ku va swakudya, nitrogen fixation, mulch, swiluva kumbe ku funengeta misava. Ximila xin'we xi nga endla mintirho yo hlayanyana. Eku heleni, hlela guild, hlamusela ndlela leyi swisaleli swi phamelaka misava swakudya ha yona, u tlhela u endla xiboho xa leswaku hi swihi support plants leswi u faneleke ku swi hlayisa, ku swi tsema kumbe ku swi susa. Hi wihi ntirho lowu ha pfumalaka?
body.backTranslation: Choose guild members to be food, nitrogen fixation, mulch, flowers or soil cover. One plant can do several jobs. At the end, plan the guild, explain how the crop remains feed the soil, and decide which support plants you should keep, cut or remove. Which job is still missing?

english.heading: Look for Root Nodules
body: Legumes work with rhizobia in nodules on their roots.

heading.backTranslation: Look for Nodules on the Roots

body.text: Legumes swi tirha swin'we ni rhizobia eka nodules etimitsini ta swona.
body.backTranslation: Legumes work together with rhizobia at the nodules on their roots.

english.heading: Look for Root Nodules
body: These bacteria convert nitrogen from the air into forms the legume can use.  Find nodules on a spare legume plant. Nodulation and growth depend on the plant, suitable bacteria and growing conditions. Can you find the nodules?

heading.backTranslation: Look for Nodules on the Roots

body.text: Bakteriya (bacteria) leti ti hundzuluxa nitrogen leyi humaka emoyeni ku va swivumbeko leswi legume yi nga swi tirhisaka. Kuma nodules eka ximila xa legume lexi nga lavekiki. Nodulation ni ku kula swi titshege hi ximila, bakteriya (bacteria) leti faneleke ni swiyimo swa ku kula. Xana u nga kuma nodules?
body.backTranslation: Bacteria that convert nitrogen from the air into forms that the legume can use. Find nodules on a legume plant that is not required/needed. Nodulation and growth depend on the plant, the right bacteria and the growing conditions. Can you find nodules?

english.heading: Return Leaves to the Soil
body: Nitrogen in plant material becomes useful as that material breaks down.

body.text: Nitrogen leyi nga eka swilo swa swimila yi va yi pfunaka loko swilo leswo swi bola.
body.backTranslation: The nitrogen in plant material becomes helpful when that material rots.

english.heading: Return Leaves to the Soil
body: Return suitable leafy prunings, fallen leaves and crop residues as mulch. Soil organisms release nutrients during decomposition.  This takes time. A living legume is not an instant fertiliser pipe into the fruit tree. Which residues can you return?

body.text: Vuyisela matluka lama tsemiweke lama faneleke, matluka lama wileke ni swisaleli swa swibyariwa tanihi mulch. Swivumbiwa swa le misaveni swi humesa nutrients hi nkarhi wa decomposition. Leswi swi teka nkarhi. Legume leyi hanyaka a hi payipi ya manyoro ya xihatla leyi yaka eka murhi wa mihandzu. Hi swihi swisaleli leswi u nga swi vuyiselaka?
body.backTranslation: Return suitable cut leaves, fallen leaves and crop residues as mulch. Things from the soil release nutrients during decomposition. This takes time. A living legume is not a fast fertiliser pipe going to a fruit tree. Which residues can you return?

english.heading: Sesbania Has a Useful Role
body: Sesbania sesban can supply fast growth and leafy mulch.

heading.text: Sesbania Yi Ni Ntirho Wo Pfuna

body.text: Sesbania sesban yi nga nyika ku kula hi xihatla ni mulch wa matluka.
body.backTranslation: Sesbania sesban can give quick growth and leaf mulch.

english.heading: Sesbania Has a Useful Role
body: It is indigenous to KwaZulu-Natal. In suitable warm conditions, manage this short-lived shrub or small tree as a support plant.  Allow room for its growth. Prune for mulch and reassess it when shade or water competition increases. Where could you manage its growth?

heading.text: Sesbania Yi Ni Ntirho Wo Pfuna

body.text: Yi indigenous eka KwaZulu-Natal. Eka swiyimo leswi faneleke swa ku hisa, lawula xihlahla lexi hanyaka nkarhi wo koma kumbe murhi lowuntsongo tanihi support plant. Siya ndhawu yo kula ka yona. Tsema marhavi ya yona ku endla mulch u tlhela u yi kambisisa nakambe loko ndzhuti kumbe ku phikizana ka mati swi engeteleka. Xana u nga lawula ku kula ka yona kwihi?
body.backTranslation: It is indigenous to KwaZulu-Natal. In suitable warm conditions, manage it as a short-lived shrub or a small tree as a support plant. Leave room for it to grow. Cut its branches to make mulch and check it again if shade or water competition increases. Where can you manage its growth?

english.heading: Check the Full Plant Name
body: Sesbania sesban and Sesbania punicea are different species.

heading.text: Kambela Vito Leri Heleleke Ra Ximila
heading.backTranslation: Check the Full Name of the Plant

body.text: Sesbania sesban na Sesbania punicea i mixaka leyi hambaneke ya swimila.
body.backTranslation: Sesbania sesban and Sesbania punicea are different kinds of plants.

english.heading: Check the Full Plant Name
body: Sesbania punicea is the invasive red sesbania. Its pods have four lengthwise wings. Confirm identity using reliable botanical guidance.  Check the full name before planting. Respect the agreed project species list, including any restriction on Sesbania sesban. Can the supplier verify the species?

heading.text: Kambela Vito Leri Heleleke Ra Ximila
heading.backTranslation: Check the Full Name of the Plant

body.text: Sesbania punicea i red sesbania leyi invasive. Swikhumba swa yona swa mbewu (pods) swi ni tipapa ta mune leti leha hi ku leha ka xikhumba. Tiyisisa leswaku i xihi hi ku tirhisa botanical guidance leyi tshembekaka. Kambisisa vito hinkwaro ku nga si byala. Xixima project species list leyi pfumeleriweke, ku katsa ni nsivelo wihi na wihi eka Sesbania sesban. Xana muphakeri a nga tiyisisa leswaku i xihi ximila?
body.backTranslation: Sesbania punicea is the invasive red sesbania. Its seed pods have four wings running along the length of the pod. Make sure which one it is by using reliable botanical guidance. Check the whole name before planting. Respect the approved project species list, including any restriction on Sesbania sesban. Can the supplier confirm which plant it is?

english.heading: Pigeon Pea Gives Food Too
body: Pigeon pea—Cajanus cajan—can provide peas, leafy material and nitrogen fixation.

heading.text: Pigeon Pea Na Yona Yi Nyika Swakudya

body.text: Pigeon pea—Cajanus cajan—yi nga nyika tinyawa (peas), swilo swa matluka ni nitrogen fixation.
body.backTranslation: Pigeon pea (Cajanus cajan) can give peas, leaf material and nitrogen fixation.

english.heading: Pigeon Pea Gives Food Too
body: Use a sunny, freely draining position. It is a short-lived support shrub; frost and waterlogging can limit it.  Decide whether each plant mainly supplies peas or leafy material. Frequent severe cutting can damage it and reduce the food harvest. Are you growing this plant for peas or mulch?

heading.text: Pigeon Pea Na Yona Yi Nyika Swakudya

body.text: Tirhisa ndhawu leyi nga ni dyambu laha mati ma hundzaka kahle ekhatsi ka misava. I support shrub leyi hanyaka nkarhi wo koma; xiqhwa (frost) ni ku yima ka mati emisaveni swi nga yi hunguta ku kula. Endla xiboho xa leswaku ximila xin'wana ni xin'wana xi ta nyika tinyawa (peas) hi ku tala kumbe swilo swa matluka. Ku xi tsema hi matimba minkarhi yo tala swi nga xi onha, swi tlhela swi hunguta ntshovelo wa swakudya. Xana u byala ximila lexi ku kuma tinyawa kumbe mulch?
body.backTranslation: Use a sunny place where water drains well through the soil. It is a short-lived support shrub; frost and standing water in the soil can reduce its growth. Decide whether each plant will mainly give peas or leaf material. Cutting it hard many times can damage it and also reduce the food harvest. Do you plant this plant to get peas or mulch?

english.heading: Choose for Place and Size
body: A useful support tree in one place may be too large or unsuitable in another.

body.text: Support tree leyi pfunaka ndhawu yin'wana yi nga va yikulu ngopfu kumbe yi nga faneleki ndhawu yin'wana.
body.backTranslation: A support tree that helps one site can be too big or not suitable for another site.

english.heading: Choose for Place and Size
body: Compare mature crown, roots, shade, rainfall and temperature. Check locally appropriate species and planting rules.  Put large support trees where they have space. For a small young guild, a manageable shrub may be easier to maintain. How large will this plant become?

body.text: Fananisa crown leyi kuleke, timitsu, ndzhuti, mpfula ni ku hisa kumbe ku titimela. Kambela mixaka leyi faneleke ndhawu ya laha ni milawu ya ku byala. Veka support trees leti kulu laha ti nga ni ndhawu. Eka guild yitsongo leyi ntshwa, xihlahla lexi nga lawuleka xi nga olova ku xi hlayisa. Xana ximila lexi xi ta va xikulu ku fika kwihi?
body.backTranslation: Compare a grown crown, roots, shade, rain and heat or shelter [?]. Check the kinds that suit the site here and the rules of planting. Put big support trees where they have space. For a small new guild, a shrub that can be controlled may be easier to look after. How big will this plant become, up to where?

english.heading: Annual Cover Has a Place
body: Sunn hemp can cover a suitable warm-season gap before the next crop.

heading.text: Annual Cover Yi Ni Ndhawu Ya Yona

body.text: Sunn hemp yi nga funengeta ndhawu leyi nga riki na swilo hi nkarhi wa ku hisa lowu faneleke, ku nga si va xibyariwa lexi landzelaka.
body.backTranslation: Sunn hemp can cover ground that has no things on it during a suitable hot season, before the next crop comes.

english.heading: Annual Cover Has a Place
body: Grow it where its season and space fit the plan. Its contribution depends on growth, nodulation and the material returned.  After cutting, allow for decomposition. An annual cover crop plays a different role from a longer-lived support shrub. When will this space be needed again?

heading.text: Annual Cover Yi Ni Ndhawu Ya Yona

body.text: Yi byale laha nkarhi wa yona ni ndhawu swi fambisanaka ni ku hlela. Mpfuno wa yona wu titshege hi ku kula, nodulation ni swilo leswi vuyiseriweke. Endzhaku ka ku yi tsema, siyela nkarhi wa decomposition. Annual cover crop yi endla ntirho wo hambana ni support shrub leyi hanyaka nkarhi wo leha. Xana ndhawu leyi yi ta lavekela rini nakambe?
body.backTranslation: Plant it where its time and place fit with the plan. Its help depends on growth, nodulation and the material returned. After cutting it, allow time for decomposition. An annual cover crop does a different job from a long-lived support shrub. When will this place be needed again?

english.heading: Leave Room Around the Tree
body: Keep the young fruit tree in light and retain access for care.

body.text: Hlayisa murhi wa mihandzu lowuntshwa wu ri eka ku vonakala ka dyambu, u tlhela u siya ndlela yo fikelela yo wu khathalela.
body.backTranslation: Keep the young fruit tree in the sunlight, and leave a way of access to tend it.

english.heading: Leave Room Around the Tree
body: Keep an open establishment basin and access to the fruit tree. Place temporary support plants where their size and water use can be managed.  Put leafy cuttings where mulch is needed. Neighbouring fruit trees can share support strips between them. Can you reach both plants as they grow?

body.text: Hlayisa establishment basin yi pfulekile ni ndlela yo fikelela murhi wa mihandzu. Veka support plants ta nkarhi wo koma laha vukulu ni ku tirhisa ka tona mati swi nga lawuriwaka. Veka matluka lama tsemiweke laha mulch yi lavekaka. Mirhi ya mihandzu leyi tshamaka ekusuhi yi nga avelana support strips leti nga exikarhi ka yona. Xana u nga fikelela swimila swimbirhi leswi loko swi ya swi kula?
body.backTranslation: Keep the establishment basin open with access to the fruit tree. Put long-lived support plants where their size and water use can be managed. Put cut leaves where mulch is needed. Fruit trees that stand close together may share support strips between them. Can you reach these two plants as they grow?

english.heading: Build a Layered Support Guild
body: Combine seasonal cover, support shrubs and temporary small trees.

heading.backTranslation: Build a Support Guild Of Layers (layers)

body.text: Hlanganisa xifunengeto xa nkarhi wun'wana wa lembe, support shrubs ni mirhi yitsongo ya nkarhi wo koma.
body.backTranslation: Combine a covering of one season of the year, support shrubs and small short-lived trees.

english.heading: Build a Layered Support Guild
body: Cowpea covers sunny gaps. Pigeon pea provides food and leafy material. Managed Sesbania sesban can supply taller temporary support.  Add suitable flowering and mulch plants. Keep the mango trunk clear and manage light, water and access. Which layers fit your site?

body.text: Cowpea yi funengeta tindhawu leti pfulekeke leti nga ni dyambu. Pigeon pea yi nyika swakudya ni swilo swa matluka. Sesbania sesban leyi lawuriweke yi nga nyika support plant ya nkarhi wo koma leyi leheke ku tlula swin'wana. Engetela swimila leswi faneleke leswi nga ni swiluva ni swimila swa mulch. Hlayisa nsinya wa murhi wa mango (trunk) wu nga ri na nchumu, u lawula ku vonakala ka dyambu, mati ni ndlela yo fikelela. Hi swihi swiyenge (layers) leswi fambisanaka ni ndhawu ya wena?
body.backTranslation: Cowpea covers open areas that have sun. Pigeon pea gives food and leaf materials. Managed Sesbania sesban can give a support plant for a short period that is taller than the others. Add suitable flowering plants and mulch plants. Keep the mango tree trunk clear, controlling sunlight, water and access. Which layers fit your place?

english.heading: How Many Support Plants?
body: Plan abundant support where the site and your care can sustain it.

body.text: Hlela support plants yo tala laha ndhawu ni vuhlayisi bya wena swi nga swi kondletelaka.
body.backTranslation: Plan many support plants where your place and your care can provide for them.

english.heading: How Many Support Plants?
body: Count woody supports across the spaces between fruit trees. Sow suitable ground cover by area.  There is no universal number per fruit tree. Adjust density to water, soil, plant size and your ability to prune and thin. How much support can you maintain?

body.text: Hlaya nhlayo ya support plants leti nga swa khuni (woody) leti nga eka tindhawu hinkwato exikarhi ka mirhi ya mihandzu. Byala swimila leswi funengetaka misava leswi faneleke hi ku ya hi vukulu bya ndhawu. A ku na nhlayo yin'we leyi tirhaka hinkwako eka murhi wa mihandzu wun'wana ni wun'wana. Cinca support density hi ku ya hi mati, misava, vukulu bya swimila ni vuswikoti bya wena bya ku tsema marhavi ni ku endla thinning. Xana u nga hlayisa support plants tingani?
body.backTranslation: Count the number of woody support plants in all the spaces between the fruit trees. Plant suitable ground-covering plants according to the size of the space. There is no single number that works everywhere for every fruit tree. Change the support density according to water, soil, plant size and your ability to cut branches and do thinning. How many support plants can you keep?

english.heading: Chop-and-Drop for Light and Mulch
body: Watch the branch fall onto the cut leaves.

heading.text: Chop-and-Drop ya Ku Vonakala ka Dyambu na Mulch
heading.backTranslation: Chop-and-Drop of Sun Exposure [?] and Mulch

body.text: Languta rhavi ri wela eka matluka lama tsemiweke.
body.backTranslation: Watch a branch fall onto the cut leaves.

english.heading: Chop-and-Drop for Light and Mulch
body: Prune a support tree and return suitable leafy cuttings to the soil. The clip shows a branch cut: the support tree remains standing. Leave enough healthy foliage for the plant to recover.  Match cutting to the species. Avoid frequent severe cuts on pigeon pea, especially when growing it for peas. Which plant needs a cut—and how much?

heading.text: Chop-and-Drop ya Ku Vonakala ka Dyambu na Mulch
heading.backTranslation: Chop-and-Drop of Sun Exposure [?] and Mulch

body.text: Tsema marhavi ya support tree kutani u vuyisela misava matluka lama faneleke lama tsemiweke. Vhidiyo yi kombisa ku tsemiwa ka rhavi: support tree yi sala yi yimile. Siya matluka lama hanyaka lama ringaneke leswaku ximila xi tlhela xi tiyisa. Tsema hi ku ya hi muxaka wa ximila. Papalata ku tsema hi matimba minkarhi yo tala eka pigeon pea, ngopfu-ngopfu loko u yi byala leswaku u kuma tinyawa (peas). I ximila xihi lexi lavaka ku tsemiwa, naswona ku tsemiwa hi mpimo wihi?
body.backTranslation: Cut the branches of the support tree and return suitable cut leaves to the soil. The video shows cutting a branch: the support tree remains standing. Leave enough living leaves so the plant can recover and strengthen. Cut according to the type of plant. Avoid hard cutting many times on pigeon pea, especially when you plant it for peas. Which plant needs cutting, and cutting to what measure?

english.heading: Keep Mulch Off the Trunk
body: Spread suitable cut material over the soil, with the trunk and root collar clear.

heading.text: Hlayisa mulch kule ni nsinya wa murhi (trunk)
heading.backTranslation: Keep mulch away from the tree trunk.

body.text: Hangalasa swilo leswi tsemiweke leswi faneleke ehenhla ka misava, nsinya wa murhi (trunk) ni root collar swi nga ri na nchumu.
body.backTranslation: Spread suitable cut materials on top of the soil, keeping the trunk and root collar clear.

english.heading: Keep Mulch Off the Trunk
body: Mulch protects the surface, helps conserve moisture and returns organic material.  Leave access for watering and inspection. Cut material into manageable pieces and keep observing moisture and decomposition. Is the root collar still clear?

heading.text: Hlayisa mulch kule ni nsinya wa murhi (trunk)
heading.backTranslation: Keep mulch away from the tree trunk.

body.text: Mulch wu sirhelela misava ya le henhla, wu pfuna ku hlayisa ku tsakama ka misava naswona wu vuyisela swilo leswi humaka eka swilo leswi hanyaka. Siya ndlela yo fikelela ya ku cheleta mati ni ya ku kambisisa. Tsema swilo swi va swiphemu leswi swi nga khomekaka, u tlhela u ya emahlweni u languta ku tsakama ka misava ni decomposition. Xana root collar yi ha nga ri na nchumu?
body.backTranslation: Mulch protects the topsoil, helps to keep the moisture (wetness) of the soil, and returns things that come from living things (to the soil). Leave a way of access for watering and for checking. Cut things into pieces that can be handled, and go on looking at the moisture of the soil and the decomposition. Is the root collar still without anything (i.e. is there nothing on it / is it still clear)?

english.heading: Choose the Right Comfrey
body: Bocking 14 comfrey can supply cut leaves for mulch.

body.text: Bocking 14 comfrey yi nga nyika matluka lama tsemiweke yo endla mulch.
body.backTranslation: Bocking 14 comfrey can give cut leaves for making mulch.

english.heading: Choose the Right Comfrey
body: Obtain the correct cultivar. Bocking 14 does not spread by viable seed, but root pieces can regrow.  Place it where it has room and sufficient moisture. Cut leaves as it recovers; do not crowd the young fruit tree. Is this a good permanent place for the clump?

body.text: Kuma cultivar leyi lulameke. Bocking 14 a yi hangalali hi viable seed, kambe swiphemu swa timitsu swi nga mila nakambe. Yi veke laha yi nga ni ndhawu ni ku tsakama ka misava loku ringaneke. Tsema matluka loko yi ri karhi yi tlhela yi tiyisa; u nga yi tshiki yi phikizana ni murhi wa mihandzu lowuntshwa. Xana lexi i ndhawu leyinene leyi xihlopha xa swimila swa Bocking 14 xi nga ta tshama eka yona nkarhi hinkwawo?
body.backTranslation: Get a suitable cultivar. Bocking 14 does not spread by viable seed, but pieces of roots can grow again. Put it where it has enough space and soil moisture. Cut the leaves while it is growing and getting strong; do not let it compete with the young fruit tree. Is this a good place where the group of Bocking 14 plants can stay all the time?

english.heading: Observe Helpful Insects
body: Flowers can provide resources for useful insects.

body.text: Swiluva swi nga nyika swihlovo eka switsotswana (insects) leswi pfunaka.
body.backTranslation: Flowers can provide (food) sources for helpful insects.

english.heading: Observe Helpful Insects
body: Many ladybirds eat aphids; some parasitoid wasps attack crop pests. Flowering members such as African basil can add resources.  Watch which insects visit and whether damage changes. A flowering plant does not guarantee pest control. What is the insect actually doing?

body.text: Ladybirds to tala ti dya aphids; parasitoid wasps tin'wana ti hlasela switsotswana leswi onhaka swibyariwa (pests). Swimila leswi nga ni swiluva ku fana ni African basil swi nga engetela swihlovo. Languta switsotswana (insects) leswi endzelaka ni loko ku onhaka ku cinca. Ximila lexi nga ni swiluva a xi tiyisekisi ku lawula switsotswana leswi onhaka swibyariwa (pests). Xana xitsotswana lexi xi endla yini hakunene?
body.backTranslation: Most ladybirds eat aphids; some other parasitoid wasps attack small creatures that damage crops (pests). Plants with flowers like African basil can add sources (of food?). Watch the insects that visit and when the damage changes. A plant with flowers does not guarantee control of the small creatures that damage crops (pests). What does this insect actually do?

english.heading: Give Flowers Their Space
body: Wild garlic can be a flowering member where the site suits it.

body.text: Wild garlic yi nga va ximila lexi nga ni swiluva laha ndhawu yi yi fanelaka kona.
body.backTranslation: Wild garlic can be a flowering plant where the place suits it.

english.heading: Give Flowers Their Space
body: Tulbaghia violacea has narrow leaves and lilac flowers. Place a clump where it has light and room to grow.  Observe visiting insects. Do not promise that a ring of wild garlic will repel pests or cure an outbreak. Where can flowers grow without crowding?

body.text: Tulbaghia violacea yi ni matluka lama nga anamangiki ni swiluva leswi nga ni muhlovo wa lilac. Veka xihlopha xa swimila swa yona laha xi nga ni ku vonakala ka dyambu ni ndhawu yo kula. Languta switsotswana (insects) leswi endzelaka. U nga tshembisi leswaku xirhendzevutani xa wild garlic xi ta hlongola switsotswana leswi onhaka swibyariwa (pests) kumbe ku herisa ku hangalala ka swona. Xana swiluva swi nga kula kwihi handle ka ku phikizana?
body.backTranslation: Tulbaghia violacea has leaves that are not spreading and lilac-coloured flowers. Place a group of its plants where it has sunlight and room to grow. Watch the insects that visit. Do not promise that a border/ring of wild garlic will chase away the small creatures that damage crops (pests) or stop their spreading. Where can the flowers grow apart from competition?

english.heading: Bring the Jobs Together
body: Choose useful partners while protecting the mango's growing space.

body.text: Hlawula vanghana lava pfunaka loko u sirhelela ndhawu yo kula ya mango.
body.backTranslation: Choose helper companions when you protect the growing area of the mango.

english.heading: Bring the Jobs Together
body: Combine the support functions your site needs: nitrogen fixation, food, mulch, flowers and ground cover. Some plants serve several functions.  Keep the trunk area and path open. Reassess each member as the mango and its neighbours grow. Does each member have space and a job?

body.text: Hlanganisa support functions leswi ndhawu ya wena yi swi lavaka: nitrogen fixation, swakudya, mulch, swiluva ni swimila leswi funengetaka misava. Swimila swin'wana swi endla mintirho yo hlayanyana. Siya ndhawu leyi rhendzeleke nsinya wa murhi (trunk) ni ndlela swi pfulekile. Kambisisa nakambe ximila xin'wana ni xin'wana loko mango ni swimila leswi nga ekusuhi na yona swi ri karhi swi kula. Xana ximila xin'wana ni xin'wana xi ni ndhawu ni ntirho?
body.backTranslation: Combine the support functions that your place needs: nitrogen fixation, food, mulch, flowers and ground-covering plants. Some plants do several jobs. Leave the area around the tree trunk and the path open. Check again each plant when the mango and nearby plants are growing. Does each plant have a place and a job?

english.heading: Food Cover Also Competes
body: Sweet potato can cover ground and provide food in a suitable sunny space.

heading.text: Xakudya Lexi Funengetaka Na Xona Xa Phikizana
heading.backTranslation: Food That Also Covers and Also Competes

body.text: Sweet potato yi nga funengeta misava yi tlhela yi nyika swakudya endhawini leyi faneleke leyi nga ni dyambu.
body.backTranslation: Sweet potato can cover the soil and give food in a suitable place that has sun.

english.heading: Food Cover Also Competes
body: Keep its vines away from the young fruit tree and retain a route for care. Its roots also use water and nutrients.  Where resources are tight, compare living cover with an ordinary mulch basin. Is this cover helping the tree establish?

heading.text: Xakudya Lexi Funengetaka Na Xona Xa Phikizana
heading.backTranslation: Food That Also Covers and Also Competes

body.text: Hlayisa marhavi ya yona (vines) ma ri ekule ni murhi wa mihandzu lowuntshwa, u tlhela u siya ndlela yo khathalela. Timitsu ta yona na tona ti tirhisa mati ni nutrients. Laha swihlovo swi nga ringani, pimanisa swimila leswi funengetaka misava leswi hanyaka ni mulch basin ya ntolovelo. Xana leswi swimila swi pfuna murhi ku tshama hi ku tiyisa timitsu?
body.backTranslation: Keep its branches (vines) away from the young fruit tree, and leave a way to tend it. Its roots also use water and nutrients. Where resources are insufficient, compare living ground-covering plants with an ordinary mulch basin. Do these plants help the tree to stay with strong roots?

english.heading: First, Establish the Guild
body: Start while the young fruit tree and its support plants have enough light and water.

body.text: Sungula loko murhi wa mihandzu lowuntshwa ni support plants ta wona swi ri ni ku vonakala ka dyambu loku ringaneke ni mati lama ringaneke.
body.backTranslation: Begin when the young fruit tree and its support plants have enough sunlight and enough water.

english.heading: First, Establish the Guild
body: Plant into a suitable season, mulch and maintain establishment water. Keep the access gap open.  Start with the number of support plants you can care for. Observe survival and growth before adding more. Can you care for every plant through establishment?

body.text: Byala hi nkarhi lowu faneleke, veka mulch u tlhela u hlayisa ku cheleta mati hi nkarhi wo sungula ku mila endzhaku ka ku byala (establishment). Siya ndhawu yo fikelela yi pfulekile. Sungula hi nhlayo ya support plants leyi u nga kotaka ku yi khathalela. Languta ku hanya ni ku kula ku nga si engetela swin'wana. Xana u nga khathalela ximila xin'wana ni xin'wana hi nkarhi hinkwawo wa ku sungula ku mila?
body.backTranslation: Plant at a suitable time, put on mulch and keep up watering during the early growth period after planting (establishment). Leave the access area open. Begin with a number of support plants that you can manage to care for. Watch survival and growth before adding more. Can you care for each plant at all times in the early growth period?

english.heading: Thin as the Fruit Tree Grows
body: When pruning is no longer enough, reduce selected support plants. Cut down selected competing supports to open space. Suitable cut material can stay as mulch: this is thinning through chop-and-drop.  Manage regrowth to keep the opening. Check light, soil moisture and growth; thinning does not instantly stop root competition. Which support plants should now give way?

heading.text: Thinning Loko Murhi Wa Mihandzu Wu Kula
heading.backTranslation: Thinning When the Fruit Tree Grows

body.text: Loko ku tsema marhavi ku nga ha ringani, hunguta support plants leti hlawuriweke. Tsema ehansi support plants leti phikizanaka leti hlawuriweke ku pfula ndhawu. Swilo leswi tsemiweke leswi faneleke swi nga sala tanihi mulch: leswi i thinning hi chop-and-drop. Lawula ku mila nakambe ku hlayisa ndhawu leyi pfuleke. Kambisisa ku vonakala ka dyambu, ku tsakama ka misava ni ku kula; thinning a yi herisi hi ku hatlisa-hatlisa ku phikizana ka timitsu. I support plants tihi leti nga fanela ku tshika ndhawu sweswi?
body.backTranslation: When cutting branches is no longer enough, reduce the selected support plants. Cut down the competing selected support plants to open space. Cut material that is suitable can remain as mulch: this is thinning by chop-and-drop. Manage regrowth to keep the area open. Check sunlight, soil moisture and growth; thinning does not quickly end competition between roots. Which support plants should leave the place now?

english.heading: Move Support Into the Light
body: As shade increases, renew sun-loving support plants in open edges and younger plantings.

heading.text: Fambisa Support Plants Eka Ku Vonakala ka Dyambu
heading.backTranslation: Move Support Plants To Sun Exposure [?]

body.text: Loko ndzhuti wu engeteleka, tlhela u byala support plants leti rhandzaka dyambu emakumu lama pfulekeke ni eka swibyariwa leswintshwa.
body.backTranslation: When shade increases, plant support plants that like the sun again at the open edges and in the new plantings.

english.heading: Move Support Into the Light
body: Carry useful prunings back to established trees. Keep nearby plants only where they still perform well.  Mature fruit trees still need nutrients. Monitor growth, harvest and soil conditions; support plants do not remove that need. Where is the next useful sunny space?

heading.text: Fambisa Support Plants Eka Ku Vonakala ka Dyambu
heading.backTranslation: Move Support Plants To Sun Exposure [?]

body.text: Rhwala swilo leswi tsemiweke leswi pfunaka u swi tlherisela eka mirhi leyi simekeke. Hlayisa swimila leswi nga ekusuhi ntsena laha swi ha tirhaka kahle kona. Mirhi ya mihandzu leyi kuleke yi ha lava nutrients. Languta ku kula, ntshovelo ni swiyimo swa misava; support plants a swi susi xilaveko lexi. Xana i kwihi ndhawu leyi landzelaka leyi pfunaka leyi nga ni dyambu?
body.backTranslation: Carry the useful cut material and return it to the established trees. Keep nearby plants only where they are still working well. Grown fruit trees still need nutrients. Watch growth, harvest and soil conditions; support plants do not remove this need. Which is the next helpful sunny place?

english.heading: Let Observation Decide
body: Keep a short record of how the guild performs.

heading.text: A Leswi U Swi Vonaka Swi Endle Xiboho
heading.backTranslation: What You See Made the Decision

body.text: Tsala rhekhodo yo koma ya ndlela leyi guild yi tirhaka ha yona.
body.backTranslation: Write a short record of how the guild works.

english.heading: Let Observation Decide
body: Check fruit-tree growth, shade, soil moisture, useful harvests and pest damage. Note what was cut, returned or removed.  Use these observations to change the layout and care. A plant earns its place through what it does here. What evidence would make you change the guild?

heading.text: A Leswi U Swi Vonaka Swi Endle Xiboho
heading.backTranslation: What You See Made the Decision

body.text: Kambisisa ku kula ka murhi wa mihandzu, ndzhuti, ku tsakama ka misava, ntshovelo wo pfuna ni ku onhiwa hi switsotswana leswi onhaka swibyariwa (pests). Tsala leswi tsemiweke, leswi vuyiseriweke kumbe leswi susiweke. Tirhisa leswi u swi voneke ku cinca ndlela leyi swimila swi vekiwaka ha yona ni ndlela leyi u swi khathalelaka ha yona. Ximila xi kuma ndhawu ya xona hi leswi xi swi endlaka laha. I vumbhoni byihi lebyi nga ku endlaka u cinca guild?
body.backTranslation: Check the growth of the fruit tree, shade, soil moisture, helpful harvest and damage by insects that damage crops (pests). Write down what has been cut, returned or removed. Use what you have seen to change how the plants are placed and how you care for them. A plant gets its place by what it does there. What evidence makes you change a guild?

english.heading: Plan One Real Guild
body: Choose one fruit tree and mark a layout you can manage.

body.text: Hlawula murhi wun'we wa mihandzu u tlhela u kombisa ndlela yo vekisa leyi u nga yi lawulaka.
body.backTranslation: Choose one fruit tree and show a way of placing that you can control.

english.heading: Plan One Real Guild
body: Record the tree, site conditions and missing jobs. Name the support species fully, mark the starting number and leave access.  Write down what will trigger pruning or thinning. Agree the species list with the project team where required. Can someone else explain your plan back to you?

body.text: Tsala murhi, swiyimo swa ndhawu ni mintirho leyi pfumalaka. Thya mavito ya support species hi ku helela, kombisa nhlayo yo sungula u tlhela u siya ndlela yo fikelela. Tsala leswi nga ta endla leswaku ku tsemiwa marhavi kumbe thinning. Pfumelelana hi species list ni ntlawa wa phurojeke laha swi lavekaka kona. Xana munhu un'wana a nga ku hlamuselela nakambe pulani ya wena?
body.backTranslation: Write down the tree, the site conditions and the missing functions. Name the support species in full, show the starting number and leave an access way. Write down what will lead to branch cutting or thinning. Agree on the species list with the project group where needed. Can someone else explain your plan back to you?

english.heading: Plant, Observe, Adjust
body: Start one suitable guild and care for it through its first stage.

body.text: Sungula guild yin'we leyi faneleke, u yi hlayisa ku fika emakumu ka nkarhi wa yona wo sungula.
body.backTranslation: Start one suitable guild, and look after it until the end of its starting time.

english.heading: Plant, Observe, Adjust
body: Use the right species, a manageable number of plants and room to grow. Return useful biomass and protect the fruit tree.  Review the planting as crowns expand. Keep, cut, replace or remove each support plant when its role changes. What will you do first—and when will you review it?

body.text: Tirhisa muxaka wa ximila lowu faneleke, nhlayo leyi nga lawuriwaka ya swimila ni ndhawu yo kula. Vuyisela biomass leyi pfunaka u tlhela u sirhelela murhi wa mihandzu. Kambela nakambe ku byala loko crowns ti ri karhi ti anama. Hlayisa, tsema, cinca hi yin'wana kumbe susa support plant yin'wana ni yin'wana loko ntirho wa yona wu cinca. I yini leswi u nga ta swi endla ku sungula, naswona u ta yi kambela nakambe rini?
body.backTranslation: Use a suitable type of plant, a manageable number of plants and room to grow. Return helpful biomass and protect the fruit tree. Re-check the planting when the crowns are spreading. Keep, cut, swap for another, or remove any support plant when its function changes. What will you do to begin, and when will you re-check it?
